answers.explanation: The writer disputes the popular view that electricity from living cells is novel, so the posture is contentious.
The passage says early bio cells were powered with sugar, so they initially derived their energy from sugar.
The passage says bio cells may use materials that would otherwise be waste, giving a cheap source of energy.
The passage says people experienced the shock from fish before electricity was really discovered.
The writer urges guarding the mind, saying evil thoughts may come but there is virtue in keeping them out.
The first paragraph warns that if thoughts are not controlled they will become our enemies and drag us to ruin.
The argument compares those who dwell on evil to someone turning a morsel over, so evil thoughts control those who treasure them.
The expression warns that dwelling on evil thoughts leads to evil deeds, so uncontrolled thoughts may lead to wrongdoing.
The fourth paragraph argues that each wave of wicked thought adds to corruption, so the more evil we think, the viler we become.
Inclinations means tendencies or natural leanings.
The passage says people eat and wear clothes because they understand the consequences of not doing so.
The passage says management decisions are based on assumptions, so all such decisions rest on assumptions.
